prompt.en: In Steward's experiment, carrot phloem cells grew into a complete carrot plant. Describe the two changes the cells went through. Use the words dedifferentiate and redifferentiate.

level1.en: What did the phloem cells have to regain first, before anything else could happen?

clue.en: To dedifferentiate is to regain the ability to divide. The cells then formed a mass of unspecialised cells.

level2Template.en: First, the phloem cells dedifferentiated: they regained the ability to ___ and formed a mass of unspecialised cells.

level1.en: What did the mass of unspecialised cells form when it was grown in the right conditions?

clue.en: To redifferentiate is to change again into cells with special jobs. The mass formed roots and a shoot.

level2Template.en: Then the cells redifferentiated to form roots, a ___ and finally a complete plant.

text.en: First, the phloem cells dedifferentiated: they regained the ability to divide and formed an undifferentiated mass of unspecialised cells.
Then, in the right conditions, the cells redifferentiated: they changed again to form roots, a shoot and finally a complete plant.
